results.name: tens_sets_nonround_targets
results.description: For sets of >= 2 examples that are all multiples of 10, yes-rate for targets that are not multiples of 10; observed > null means people accept non-round numbers for all-round sets more than the model's strong multiples-of-10 rule predicts (observed < null: they reject them more).
results.code:
# name: tens_sets_nonround_targets
# description: For sets of >= 2 examples that are all multiples of 10, yes-rate for targets that are not multiples of 10; observed > null means people accept non-round numbers for all-round sets more than the model's strong multiples-of-10 rule predicts (observed < null: they reject them more).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    allten = np.where(np.isnan(ex), True, np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10 == 0).all(axis=1)
    mask = (n >= 2) & allten & (t % 10 != 0)
    return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.any() else 0.0

results.name: single_digit_targets_for_high_sets
results.description: For sets whose smallest example is >= 20, yes-rate for single-digit targets (1-9); observed > null means people accept small one-digit numbers for high-valued sets more than the model's rules/intervals predict (observed < null: they treat one-digit numbers as a separate category and reject them more than the model).
results.code:
# name: single_digit_targets_for_high_sets
# description: For sets whose smallest example is >= 20, yes-rate for single-digit targets (1-9); observed > null means people accept small one-digit numbers for high-valued sets more than the model's rules/intervals predict (observed < null: they treat one-digit numbers as a separate category and reject them more than the model).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    mn = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    mask = (mn >= 20) & (t <= 9)
    return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.any() else 0.0

results.name: singleton_same_decade_contrast
results.description: For single-example sets, among targets within 9 of the example (excluding the example), yes-rate for targets in the same decade (same tens digit, 100 counted with 90s) minus yes-rate for targets in a different decade; observed > null means people generalize along decade categories beyond what distance-matched intervals in the model predict (observed < null: decades matter less than modelled).
results.code:
# name: singleton_same_decade_contrast
# description: For single-example sets, among targets within 9 of the example (excluding the example), yes-rate for targets in the same decade (same tens digit, 100 counted with 90s) minus yes-rate for targets in a different decade; observed > null means people generalize along decade categories beyond what distance-matched intervals in the model predict (observed < null: decades matter less than modelled).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    x = np.nan_to_num(ex[:, 0]).astype(int)
    dec = lambda v: np.minimum(v, 99) // 10
    near = (n == 1) & (np.abs(t - x) <= 9) & (t != x)
    same = near & (dec(t) == dec(x))
    diff = near & (dec(t) != dec(x))
    if not same.any() or not diff.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[same].mean() - r[diff].mean())

results.name: small_sets_large_targets
results.description: For sets of >= 2 examples that are all <= 10, yes-rate for targets > 20; observed > null means people extend small-number sets to large numbers (via rules like odd/multiples) more than the model predicts (observed < null: they stay confined to small numbers more than the model).

    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()

results.name: tight_pair_near_outside
results.description: For 2-example sets with range <= 10, yes-rate for targets outside [min,max] but within 10 of the nearest example; observed > null means people extend a tight pair to nearby numbers more than the model's size-principle intervals predict (observed < null: they generalize beyond a tight pair less than the model).
results.code:
# name: tight_pair_near_outside
# description: For 2-example sets with range <= 10, yes-rate for targets outside [min,max] but within 10 of the nearest example; observed > null means people extend a tight pair to nearby numbers more than the model's size-principle intervals predict (observed < null: they generalize beyond a tight pair less than the model).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    lo, hi = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(lo - t, t - hi)
    mask = (n == 2) & (hi - lo <= 10) & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 10)
    return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.any() else 0.0

results.name: outlier_sets_in_range_nonrule
results.description: For 4-example sets where exactly 3 examples share a last digit and the 4th does not (e.g. 92,82,27,42; 71,61,26,81), yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside [min,max] that lack the shared last digit; observed > null means people abandon the near-fitting rule for a range spanning all examples more than the model's inferred stray tolerance predicts (observed < null: they keep the rule and treat the odd example as a stray more than the model).
results.code:
# name: outlier_sets_in_range_nonrule
# description: For 4-example sets where exactly 3 examples share a last digit and the 4th does not (e.g. 92,82,27,42; 71,61,26,81), yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside [min,max] that lack the shared last digit; observed > null means people abandon the near-fitting rule for a range spanning all examples more than the model's inferred stray tolerance predicts (observed < null: they keep the rule and treat the odd example as a stray more than the model).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    if ex.shape[1] < 4:
        return 0.0
    n = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    dig = np.where(np.isnan(ex), -1, np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10)
    counts = np.stack([(dig == k).sum(axis=1) for k in range(10)], axis=1)
    has3 = (counts == 3).any(axis=1) & (n == 4)
    maj = counts.argmax(axis=1)
    lo, hi = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    is_ex = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    mask = has3 & (t % 10 != maj) & ~is_ex & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.any() else 0.0

results.name: pair_wide_gap_in_range
results.description: For 2-example sets with range >= 20 whose examples share no last digit and no common factor >= 3, yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside [min,max]; observed > null means people fill the gap between two unrelated distant examples more than the model's interval/rule mixture predicts (observed < null: less).
results.code:
# name: pair_wide_gap_in_range
# description: For 2-example sets with range >= 20 whose examples share no last digit and no common factor >= 3, yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside [min,max]; observed > null means people fill the gap between two unrelated distant examples more than the model's interval/rule mixture predicts (observed < null: less).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    a = np.nan_to_num(ex[:, 0]).astype(int)
    b = np.nan_to_num(ex[:, 1]).astype(int) if ex.shape[1] > 1 else np.zeros_like(a)
    g = np.gcd(a, b)
    lo, hi = np.minimum(a, b), np.maximum(a, b)
    ok = (n == 2) & (hi - lo >= 20) & (a % 10 != b % 10) & (g < 3)
    mask = ok & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.any() else 0.0

results.name: within_set_cell_spread
results.description: For sets asked about with >= 5 distinct targets, the standard deviation of per-target yes-rates within the set, averaged across sets; observed > null means people's generalization within a set is sharper / more all-or-none across targets than the model predicts (observed < null: flatter, more graded than the model).
